itens.descricao: Palantir Guided for $2.16 Billion in Revenue for Q3. Its Last 2 Quarters Suggest We Should Expect More. Yahoo Finance
trechos: Palantir Guided for $2.16 Billion in Revenue for Q3.
Its Last 2 Quarters Suggest We Should Expect More.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has been one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with its stock gaining more than 1,000% over the last three years.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
"Act 2" is the global rollout.
Continue » The company's guidance was for third-quarter revenue between $2.160 billion and $2.164 billion, which would amount to another impressive quarter of growth.
In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if Palantir delivers more than $2.3 billion in revenue, easily surpassing its own expectations.

itens.descricao: Independentemente de governo, se eu estivesse sentado lá manteria FGI/FGO, é ótimo programa, diz CEO do Bradesco Valor Econômico
trechos: “É natural que enquanto a gente estiver crescendo ele vá influenciar cada vez mais o ‘over 90’ e que vá chamar um custo de provisão”, disse, acrescentando que, para essa curva começar a cair, “é uma questão de tempo”.

“Eu sinceramente custo a acreditar numa medida muito dura vinda do Banco Central, mas é uma percepção pessoal minha em relação a isso.”  O banco também comentou medidas para redução de custos e ganhos de eficiência.
Cassiano Scarpelli, vice-presidente financeiro do Bradesco, afirmou que o banco está chegando perto do “ajuste ótimo” da rede de agências.

trechos: This Underappreciated Nvidia-Backed Company Is Growing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Revenue by 123%.
Here's Why It's a Buy Today for $8.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
The semiconductor giant invested $1 billion in Nokia last year, establishing a framework that stands to reshape the telecommunications industry.
How Nokia is evolving from phones to AI Last October, Nvidia invested $1 billion in Nokia, acquiring 2.9% of the company.
This process is known as edge AI, and according to data compiled by Omdia, the AI-RAN market is expected to exceed $200 billion by 2030.
Nokia's earnings reveal where the real growth is happening During the third quarter, Nokia generated 5.2 billion euros in revenue.

itens.titulo: Brent crude oil tops $116, a six-month high, as tensions swell in the Middle East
itens.descricao: Brent crude oil tops $116, a six-month high, as tensions swell in the Middle East CNBC
trechos: Brent futures were up 2.6% at $116.13 a barrel, the highest level for the international benchmark since April 30.
West Texas Intermediate traded about 3% higher at $102.56 a barrel.
Iran's army chief, meanwhile, said the country's military is fully prepared for "asymmetric warfare" after strengthening its capabilities, according to the state media agency Tasnim.
Brent futures were on track for a weekly rise of nearly 6%, putting the contracts on course for their third consecutive week of gains.
WTI futures were on track for a weekly gain of 1%.

itens.titulo: Tesla Fell 3% as Musk Trims Capex, Delays Optimus Ramp for “The Biggest Product on Earth”
itens.descricao: Tesla Fell 3% as Musk Trims Capex, Delays Optimus Ramp for “The Biggest Product on Earth” Yahoo Finance
trechos: Key Takeaways - Tesla stock fell 3% on Thursday after its third-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.48 per share beat the $0.45 analysts expected.
- Even after Tesla cut its 2026 capex budget to about $20 billion, it still plans to spend more than twice what it spent in 2025.
- Tesla's forward P/E is still far above its five-year average of 108x.
The stock fell 3% on Thursday anyway, closing at $375.
The numbers held up Adjusted earnings came in at $0.48 per share, ahead of the $0.45 analysts expected.
Plus: - Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits rose to 18.1%, from 15.4% a year earlier.
- Free cash flow swung back to $1.5 billion, after a $1.1 billion outflow in the second quarter.
- Active paid FSD customers—including upfront purchasers and monthly subscribers—climbed 67% from a year earlier, to 1.74 million.
